name: Web Performance & Accessibility
description: Making websites fast and usable by everyone, using Core Web Vitals, performance optimization techniques and WCAG accessibility practices.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the alt attribute on an element?
options: It sets the image's tooltip color
It lazy-loads the image
It provides a text alternative for screen readers and when the image fails to load
It defines the image's file format
questions.explanation: alt text conveys the image's meaning to users who cannot see it; decorative images should use alt="".

questions.question: Which Core Web Vital measures how long it takes for the largest visible content element to render?
options: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)
Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)
Interaction to Next Paint (INP)
Time to First Byte (TTFB)
questions.explanation: LCP measures loading performance by timing when the largest image or text block in the viewport is rendered.

questions.question: What is the WCAG 2 Level AA minimum contrast ratio for normal-size body text?
questions.explanation: WCAG success criterion 1.4.3 (AA) requires 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.

questions.question: Which change most directly reduces Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) caused by images?
options: Converting images to PNG
Specifying width and height attributes (or aspect-ratio) so space is reserved before the image loads
Adding more images above the fold
Loading images with JavaScript after page load
questions.explanation: Reserving dimensions lets the browser allocate space up front, so content does not jump when images arrive.

questions.question:
A developer builds a clickable
Save
. What is the best fix for accessibility?
options: Add a title attribute to the div
Add cursor: pointer in CSS
Use a native <button> element, which is focusable, keyboard-operable and announced as a button
Add aria-label="Save" to the div
questions.explanation: Native buttons provide focus, Enter/Space activation and the correct role for free; a div needs role, tabindex and key handlers to approximate this.

questions.question: What is the effect of adding the defer attribute to a <script src> tag in the document head?
options: The script is downloaded in parallel with HTML parsing and executed after parsing completes, in document order
The script is never executed
The script blocks parsing until it downloads and executes
The script executes immediately when downloaded, in any order
questions.explanation: defer avoids render-blocking: scripts download without blocking the parser and run in order after the document is parsed (async runs as soon as downloaded, in any order).

practical.title: Write an accessible, performance-friendly image and form field
practical.instructions: Write HTML for (1) a below-the-fold product photo 'shoe.jpg' that is lazy-loaded, has meaningful alt text and has explicit width (400) and height (300) to avoid layout shift; and (2) an email input with a properly associated visible label.

rubric.hint: Add descriptive alt text, e.g. alt="Red running shoe".
Use loading="lazy" for images below the fold.
Set width="400" height="300" so the browser reserves space.

rubric.description: Input is associated with a label
rubric.hint: Use <label for="email"> with a matching id on the input, or wrap the input in the label.

tasks.title: Learn accessibility and performance basics
tasks.description: Work through the first modules of web.dev Learn Accessibility and Learn Performance. Note the WCAG principles (perceivable, operable, understandable, robust) and the Core Web Vitals.
tasks.completion_criteria: Can define LCP, INP and CLS and give one example per WCAG principle.

tasks.title: Audit a page with Lighthouse
tasks.description: Run a Lighthouse audit in Chrome DevTools on one of your own pages. Fix at least five reported performance or accessibility issues and re-run the audit.
tasks.completion_criteria: Before/after Lighthouse reports showing at least five issues fixed.

tasks.title: Make a component keyboard and screen-reader friendly
tasks.description: Build an accessible modal dialog or tabs component following the ARIA Authoring Practices Guide pattern. Test it using only the keyboard and with a screen reader.
tasks.completion_criteria: Component meets the APG keyboard interaction spec, traps and restores focus correctly, and is announced properly by a screen reader.

tasks.title: Optimize a site to pass Core Web Vitals and WCAG AA
tasks.description: Take an existing multi-page site and optimize images, fonts and scripts, then remediate accessibility issues against WCAG 2.2 AA. Document each change and its measured impact.
tasks.completion_criteria: Lighthouse performance and accessibility scores of at least 90 and a written report of changes with before/after metrics.
